questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I looked through the course catalogues of a ton of universities, and ETH had the most courses that seemed interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: While it was not part of my motivation for choosing ETH, I ended up really enjoying Switzerland for its nature as well, going on a lot of hiking and ski trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Everything was communicated decently over e-mail. Had to sit through some not that great webinars as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A quick welcome presentation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I signed up for the ETH allocated housing and got it. If you do not get housing through ETH, it can be rough to find accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nothing special.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got placed in a 160 person WOKO dorm. While the social life here was awesome, toilets, common room and *especially* the kitchen were a mess. Surprised I survived 5 months without getting food poisoning to be honest.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got a mail saying registration was open, after which I could start registering for courses. I got this mail pretty late, however, so 2 of the courses I wanted to take had already been filled up by the time I was made aware I could register.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: idk

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get the course I was most interested in, but other than that I had to change my entire study plan due to scheduling conflicts and/or courses not having space for me.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get too attached to your original study plan. Be ready to adapt. Lot's of good courses to choose from, so be open minded.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I went during the 5th semester of my Bachelor and took exclusively Master's courses. The level of the courses varied greatly and was mostly a bit above what I was used to at UCPH. One course in particular had an insane, genuinely unreasonable, workload...

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: About the same. Lectures followed by exercise classes. Unlike at UCPH where exercise classes are usually split into groups of 20 students, exercise classes at ETH were held with the entire class and a few TAs in the same auditorium. The advantage of this approach was that most exercise classes had a quick (well-made) presentation by a TA. The disadvantage is that it can be difficult to get help from a TA. For some courses in particular, you had to wait a loong time before you could ask a question.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Network security
Computer Graphics
Computer Architecture
Embedded Systems

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Network Security was great. Most well-organized course I've ever taken with great content and fun projects.
Embedded Systems had an unintelligible Italian lecturer, but the exercises were good and the content was varied.
Computer Graphics was a lot of work. If you are interested in the topic, I definitely recommend it, but stay away if you only have a passing interest.

Computer Architecture was not great. Two 3-hour lectures every week with with way too much content. The workload was also quite large with 25 paper reviews on top of standard exercise sheets and some labs that could be pretty time consuming. While the research group does high quality, interesting research, you really have to put in a lot of time to not fall behind -- and time is limited on an exchange!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: e-sim -- my 3-like-home subscription did not cover my entire stay, so had to get a data e-sim after the first month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out in general is very expensive. Even cafeteria food can be a little pricey.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All ETH exchange students are members of ASVZ which has a ton of awesome facilities for all kinds of sports. I didn't have to time to make use of it as much as I would have liked.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I attended a crash course in ballroom dancing for 4 weeks. ESN also hosts a ton of cool events that I attended. (ski trip, visit to CERN, etc)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for a ton of ESN events - especially in the first week. Great way to meet people and make friends quickly.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes. I definitely didn't see myself as a nature person before this exchange, but I ended up doing a lot of hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, attend ESN events. Living in a huge WOKO dorm with lots of people also helps.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Swiss timeliness. Public transportation is always on time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go on lots of hikes (you can do 1 a week)
- Don't get completely lost in studying (within reason). Try to sign up for as many events as possible and meet new people.
- Do not take Computer Architecture unless you *really* like the area and are prepared to spend *a lot* of time on it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Hiking and meeting lots of new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing studying with wanting to go on trips.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
